• Scientific name: Neblinichthys pilosus Ferraris, Isbrücker & Nijssen, 1986
  • Common name: Punk Pleco
  • Size: 89 mm (3.5 in) SL
  • IUCN Red List: Least Concern (last assessed 2019)
  • Etymology: Neblin- is based on the Neblina camp, where the type specimen was caught. -ichthys: fish. Literally "fish from Neblina". The specific epithet refers to its hairy (pilosus = hairy) appearance.
  • Type locality: Río Mawarinuma tributary, at Neblina base camp, on the right bank in a riffle, 0°55'N, 66°10'W, Venezuela, elevation 120 m.
South America: Upper Negro, Casiquiare, and Baria River basins in Venezuela.

South America: Upper Negro, Casiquiare and Baria River basins, Venezuela. Type locality: Venezuela, Territorio Federal Amazonas; Dept. Rio Negro, Rio Baria basin. Rio Mawarinuma tributary at Neblina base camp, on right bank in riffle, 0º55'N, 66º10'W, elevation 120 m.

This species is only known from Baria River, Negro River drainage, in Amazonas state. It inhabits rapids with swift currents and rocky substrates (Armbruster and Taphorn 2013). The genus ranges across the Western Guiana Shield in small streams; however, a giant gap in the range occurs from Pico Neblina to the upper Caroni. This gap is at least partially bridged by specimens collected in the middle Río Paragua, a tributary of the Río Caroni in eastern Venezuela.

IUCN Red List: This species has a relatively restricted distribution but there are no known threats to it at present. Therefore, it is assessed as Least Concern. Threats including pollution and habitat loss might arise in the future if illegal gold mines continue to spread in the area (IUCN 2019).

Species of Neblinichthys are known for their extremely large odontodes on the snouts of nuptial males (nuptial males of N. yaravi and fully developed males of N. brevibracchium Taphorn, Armbruster, López-Fernández & Bernard, are not known), which are directed anterodorsally in N. pilosus Ferraris, Isbrücker & Nijssen and N. roraima Provenzano, Lasso & Ponte and largely anteriorly in N. echinasus Taphorn, Armbruster, López-Fernández & Bernard.

Etymology: The genus name Neblinichthys: brevis (L.), short; bracchium (L.), forearm, referring to relatively short pectoral spines present in the genus. The specific name pilosus: Latin for hairy, referring to the "hair-styled" (quotes in original) bristles of mature males.
